page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.13xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor technology. It features 52 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.38 GB of RAM per vCPU. A primary hardware attribute is its bundled local storage array comprising 11,519 GB of local SSD storage, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

The hardware configuration provides notable qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-heavy operations by eliminating external cloud storage latency through directly attached high-capacity local SSDs. Resource density remains strong across memory and storage dimensions relative to compute count. Key tradeoffs include the reliance on ephemeral local disk structures that necessitate software-level replication for durability, along with the complete absence of discrete GPU hardware for accelerated processing tasks.

Based on its 11,519 GB local SSD storage and 384.0 GB RAM capacity, ecs.i3.13xlarge is designed for large-scale transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time data analytics, enterprise search indices, and ETL pipeline processing requiring low-latency storage access.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.13xlarge is a high-density storage and database instance powered by 52 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. It includes 384.0 GB of RAM (7.38 GB per core) and features an integrated 11,519 GB local SSD storage array along with a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under the KVM hypervisor. By bundling large-capacity local SSD storage with substantial system memory, this instance provides direct physical disk access that avoids network storage latency, maximizing cost efficiency for high-throughput data operations. The primary trade-off is the reliance on local storage requiring application-level data redundancy, as well as the absence of GPU acceleration. The ecs.i3.13xlarge instance is optimal for large-scale relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, big data analytics engines, and enterprise search platforms demanding high local disk density and extensive memory caching.
